items.title: A high power of an ideal maps through the derived tensor product of the ideal with the module
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)

items.difficulty_reason: The statement says that for an ideal in a Noetherian ring and a finite module there is a positive power of the ideal whose map to the module factors through the derived tensor product of the ideal with the module (statement lines 29736-29742). Besides the short proof through the known pro-isomorphism, the author gives a direct argument that reduces the goal through a distinguished triangle to the vanishing of a composite into the derived tensor product with the quotient, factors the quotient map through the Koszul complex, and then runs a finite induction in which the obstruction to improving the factorization is an element of an Ext group of a power of the ideal with a module annihilated by the ideal, which can be killed by raising the power (proof lines 29744-29767). The two reductions and the boundedness of the Koszul complex are what turn the statement into finitely many vanishing conditions. The counted span refers twice to earlier results of this chapter, carried as navigation stubs.
